summary: cmd_list runs the existing bad_tags check on every path. Plain list and --all check the tasks they display. --overdue checks every open task (the ones it examines, as it already does for stored due dates), before filtering to the overdue ones, so a bad tags value on an open task that is not overdue or has no due date still exits 2 with 'error: task N has invalid tags: <repr>'. The --tag filter runs after the check.
assumptions: Plain list and --all validate only the tasks they would show; done tasks are unchecked on plain list.
--overdue validates all open tasks, not only the overdue ones, mirroring its existing due-date validation; the verify failure showed tasks that were not displayed must still be rejected.
